summary: Australia Awards Scholarships are long-term awards from Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade for people from developing partner countries, including Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya and 22 other African countries, to study full time at participating Australian universities and TAFE institutes.
meta_description: Australia Awards Scholarships pay full tuition, flights, a living allowance and health cover. Who can apply, what it covers and the round dates.
covers: A single return economy airfare to and from Australia.
An establishment allowance towards accommodation, textbooks and study materials.
A fortnightly Contribution to Living Expenses, at a rate the department sets.
Overseas Student Health Cover for the length of the award (for the award holder only).
A compulsory Introductory Academic Program before formal study, and pre-course English training where it is needed.
eligibility: Citizens of a participating country: in Africa these include Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Ethiopia, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe, among 25.
Undergraduate or postgraduate study, full time, at a participating Australian institution.
Willingness to sign a contract with the Commonwealth of Australia and accept the award's conditions.
how_to_apply: Find your country on DFAT's list of opening and closing dates, which names the office that runs your country's applications (Australia Awards Africa for the African countries).
Apply online during your country's window. For study starting in 2027, most countries' window ran from 1 February to 30 April 2026.
If selected, choose a participating institution and course with the Australia Awards office before the award starts.
watch_out: Scholars must leave Australia for at least two years after the scholarship ends; staying on creates a debt for the whole cost of the award.
The round for 2028 study has not been announced; DFAT publishes the dates on its opening and closing dates page.
Health cover is for the award holder only, not for family members.
